subject: BrightBank: default log capture — prompts vs generated outputs & auto-erase
messages:
From: BrightBank Security <ops@brightbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about data capture defaults (prompts vs outputs)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood's private deployment options yesterday. We have a couple of follow-ups from our info security team around default capture and deletion behavior. The questionnaire attached has the full set, but two items stood out as blockers for our procurement team:

1) Clarify whether the default hosted/private deployment captures raw user requests (prompts) by default, or only final model outputs.
2) When streaming is enabled, are partial tokens (stream buffer) persisted anywhere by default, or only the final output once the generation completes?

We also need to understand: what automatic erasure mechanisms exist (time-based TTLs, tombstone purge) and what evidence we can get to show erasure took place for an audit.

Can you provide a short summary and an example scenario (e.g., interactive chat session -> what gets stored, for how long, and how to request deletion)?

Appreciate a concise answer we can drop into our procurement RFP.

Best,
Sam Peters
Ops, BrightBank

Attachment: BrightBank_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: BrightBank Security <ops@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about data capture defaults (prompts vs outputs)

Sam — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. High level answer up front: by default we capture both the request (prompt) and the final generated output for hosted and private deployments, but there are configuration knobs and exception rules that change that behavior. Streaming buffers are transient by design and are not committed to long-term store unless the session completes and the final output is recorded.

I'll let Kim add the exact TTLs and the erasure/evidence process. Marissa — can you confirm the enterprise audit artifact we can supply for an erasure request (record IDs, timestamps, and purge logs)?

Quick example scenario (short):
- User types a prompt in an interactive session. Prompt is accepted and temporarily held in a session buffer.
- If session finishes normally, both prompt and final output are written to the tenant's artifacts store (default retention window applies).
- If the session is aborted mid-stream, transient tokens are discarded — nothing is written to the long-term store.

Will follow up with concrete retention windows and how to trigger deletion for BrightBank.

—Karthik
Director, Product 
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jun 20, 2025 at 11:03 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sam — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. High level answer up front: by default we capture both the request (prompt) and the final generated output for hosted and private deployments, but there are configuration knobs and exception rules that change that behavior.

Hi all — adding the technical specifics from the runtime and storage side. Apologies in advance for the wall of text; I tried to keep the examples concrete.

Summary (defaults):
- Requests (user prompts): captured by default and stored as "request artifacts". These are indexed for troubleshooting and quality monitoring.
- Final outputs (model answers): captured by default and stored as "response artifacts".
- Stream buffers / partial tokens: ephemeral in-memory buffers. They are not flushed to persistent storage except when the stream completes and the final output is materialized.

Default retention windows (private deployment typical defaults; hosted has similar defaults configurable by account):
- Request artifacts (prompts): 90 days TTL from write time.
- Response artifacts (final outputs): 90 days TTL from write time.
- Audit logs / tracer events: 13 months by default (immutable event store for system health).

Exceptions and overrides:
- Customers can set shorter retention via the Private Console or onboarding contracts (e.g., 30d).
- Enterprise customers can opt for an auto-purge on session end (prompt not persisted) for regulated flows. That is a configuration toggle during deployment and not enabled by default.
- Attachments referenced in a session (customer-uploaded files) keep their own retention policies; we store pointers in the artifacts store but do not duplicate large blobs unless explicitly requested.

Erasure and evidence: how we show a deletion occurred (for an audit):
- When a deletion request is initiated (API or support ticket), the system records a deletion job with a unique job id.
- The job runs and tombstones records, then physically purges them during the next scheduled purge window. Logs of the job include object ids, timestamps, and the initiating principal.
- We provide customers with a signed purge summary (CSV) and an entry in the audit log that shows job id, time started/completed, and count of objects purged.

Concrete example (interactive chat):
1) 2025-06-01T14:05Z — user submits prompt "Generate Q2 payroll summary". Prompt stored as request_artifact_abc123.
2) Streaming occurs — transient tokens are buffered in-memory; no storage write.
3) Stream completes at 14:05:07Z — final output stored as response_artifact_def456.
4) On 2025-06-10 the customer requests erasure for session id xyz. We create deletion job deljob-987; purge runs on 2025-06-11 and returns a signed CSV showing request_artifact_abc123 and response_artifact_def456 deleted.

Attachments: retention-table-quickref.csv (small CSV mapping artifact types to default TTLs) and screenshot-retention-settings.png (console toggle examples).

If BrightBank needs shorter defaults or a pre-session opt-out for prompts, we can document the exact settings and provide a deployment checklist for your infra team.

—Kimberly
Senior Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions about data capture defaults (prompts vs outputs)

Sam — following up with the agreed next steps so your procurement team can close this item: 

- Default behavior: both prompts and final outputs are captured by default (90d). Streaming buffers are transient and not persisted unless a final output is written.
- Options for BrightBank: we can set the tenant to a 30-day default or enable a pre-session opt-out (prompts not written) for regulated workflows — this requires a deploy-time flag for the private control plane.
- Audit evidence: we will provide a signed purge summary and the deletion job id for each erasure request. We can also export the job entry into your SIEM on request.

Next action: if you want the 30-day default or pre-session opt-out, reply with which option you prefer and your proposed timeline. We can attach the small config doc and run a short technical call.

Thanks — happy to book a 30-minute follow-up with the infra/security teams.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
